facts.fact: The page reports an across-all-industries average email open rate of around 42.35% in 2026, which it attributes largely to privacy changes; the page points readers to mailmend.io for open rate statistics.
facts.quote: Across all industries, the average email open rate has now climbed to around **42.35%**, largely due to those privacy changes.

facts.fact: The page says an e-commerce brand might see email open rates between 26.64% and 31.08%.
facts.quote: An e-commerce brand might see rates between **26.64%** and **31.08%**, while a retail business could hit a much healthier **38.58%**.

facts.fact: The page says a retail business could reach an email open rate of 38.58%.
facts.quote: while a retail business could hit a much healthier **38.58%**.

facts.fact: The page suggests small businesses aim for an email open rate above 30-35% as a strong starting point.
facts.quote: Aiming for a rate above **30-35%** is a strong starting point.

facts.fact: The page states that personalization can boost email opens by as much as 50%.
facts.quote: The secret weapon for small businesses is personalization, which can boost opens by as much as **50%**.

facts.fact: The page states that welcome emails have an average open rate of 83.63%.
facts.quote: These emails boast an incredible average open rate of **83.63%**.

facts.fact: The page states that the average email click-through rate across all industries in 2026 is about 1.69%.
facts.quote: Across all industries in 2026, the average email CTR hovers at a humble **1.69%**.

facts.fact: The page states that top-tier email performers often reach a click-through rate of about 3.38%.
facts.quote: Even the top-tier performers are often only hitting **3.38%**.

facts.fact: The page's illustrative campaign graphic shows an open rate of 25.7%, a click rate of 4.2%, and 10,000 emails sent.
facts.quote: An overview of email marketing performance showing open rate 25.7%, click rate 4.2%, and 10,000 emails sent.

facts.fact: The page says Apple's Mail Privacy Protection downloads email content in the background, so an email can be marked as opened whether or not the subscriber viewed it.
facts.quote: This means the email is marked as opened whether the subscriber ever looked at it or not.

facts.fact: For most small businesses, a click-through rate (CTR) between 2-3% is described as a great starting point.
facts.quote: For most small businesses, aiming for a CTR between **2-3%** is a great starting point.

facts.fact: The page states that a healthy click-to-open rate (CTOR) is around 10-11%.
The page defines click-to-open rate (CTOR) as clicks measured only among subscribers who opened the email.
facts.quote: The **Click-to-Open Rate (CTOR)** measures clicks only among the subscribers who _opened_ your email.

facts.fact: The page cites one third-party study finding that marketers using segmented campaigns saw revenue increase by as much as 760%.
facts.quote: One study found that marketers using segmented campaigns saw revenue increase by as much as **760%**.
